messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] Incremental builds with macOS 27.2 may be broken
messages.subject_clean: Incremental builds with macOS 27.2 may be broken
messages.body_plain:
If you want to update a build of R-devel or R-patched after svn up. 
first look near the bottom of file Makeconf.  If the .c.d rule is NOT

.c.d:
         @echo "making $@ from $<"
         @$(CC) -MM $(ALL_CPPFLAGS) $< > $@

then you need to do a clean build, starting with make distclean and 
configure.

The clang in the 27.2 CLT/Xcode distribution has changed the format of 
the output of clang -MM (and -M) and it no longer is what configure used 
to expect, so it does not find a working .c.d rule, and all the 
Makefiles need to be remade to add missing dependencies.

We know that this was changed after CLT 26.6: we think after CLT 27 
(there was no 27.1).

-- 
Brian D. Ripley,                  ripleybd at icloud.com
Emeritus Professor of Applied Statistics, University of Oxford

Hi Jos?,

Did you by any chance update macOS on your machine recently? A guess
is that you might need to reinstall XQuartz after your update, then
restart (or log out and log in) to make sure the relevant XQuartz
login agents are running.

The output of launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/org.xquartz.startx from a
Terminal may also be helpful.

Similarly, the output of

Sys.getenv("DISPLAY")
library(tcltk)
library(tcltk2)
packageVersion("tcltk2")
packageVersion("Rcmdr")

from your RStudio session (including warnings, if any) would be useful too.

Best,
Kevin

This is the first time I see this behavior since I started working with Rcmdr years ago. I tried running Rcmdr directly from R, but R freezes. I recently upgraded to MacOS 27 Golden Gate. All I can tell is that there seems to be a problem with tcltk.

No, with package tcltk2.

This works for me with macOS 27.2.1, and I have not needed to re-install 
XQuartz for a long time.  But do check you have an X11 server running, 
as this infinite-looping behaviour is seen on Linux with tcltk2 if none 
is.  (I think the idea is that a server is auto-started on macOS, but 
that has been known to fail.)

This is a package issue, so ultimately take it up with the maintainer 
(except the CRAN page says he is uncontactable at the address in the 
package,but he seems to be active on GitHub).

messages.body_plain:
I was doing $bad_things$  with gmp, in particular  `as.bigq()` and the `%%`
method for bigz objects.  I was generating ever larger integers; at roughly
400 million digits something in the gmp lib goes wrong; returns the error
message "Error in `[<-.bigq`(`**tmp**`, jt + 1, value = as.raw(c(0x01,
0x00, 0x00, :
  negative length vectors are not allowed"

That function crash  also left around 15G of memory leaked.

But I'm not here to ask about fixing gmp.  The strange thing is that I
tried running `traceback()` and R hung.  It was chewing up CPU time as well
as grabbing gigabytes of RAM.    What could cause this behavior?  Is it
possible that `traceback` is plowing thru that 15G of leak?

I'm not an expert on dealing with memory leaks, so apologize if there's a
way to access or analyze its contents from the R command line.


Details: iMac M4 Sequoia 15.7.9     R 4.6.1 via  R.app .


regards,

Carl

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] What can make `traceback` hang?
messages.body_plain:
traceback() does print all the calls in the stack, so if you have a
veeeeeeeeeeery long call there (typically because you're using call()
or do.call() or similar), you can have problems.

f <- function(...) {
  stop("Bad")
}
g <- function(...) {
  f(...)
}

args <- setNames(rep(list(strrep("x", 20)), 26), letters)
cl <- do.call(call, c("g", args))
eval(cl)
traceback()
#> 5: stop("Bad") at example.R#2
#> 4: f(...) at example.R#5

messages.body_snippet:
traceback() does print all the calls in the stack, so if you have a
veeeeeeeeeeery long call there (typically because you're using call()
or do.call() or similar), you can have problems.

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Mac] What can make `traceback` hang?
messages.body_plain:
I’m not an expert either, but this feels similar to a hang I recently saw and initially suspected the {future} package but that we eventually attributed to processing of a large call stack: https://gist.github.com/infotroph/18d49399c4ab41ab44f341c3592b835b

In my case I was inefficiently rolling my own traceback-like messages with `limitedLabels(sys.calls)`, which best I can tell doesn’t share any code paths with traceback() but it wouldn’t surprise me if their basic limits were similar. 

No promises that this is useful, but maybe a direction to explore.

Thanks,
Chris
